method_description: Per-paper generate -> critique -> narrow (loop.md 28.1, 28.3). For the research question, the 10 most relevant papers published before the knowledge cutoff are retrieved. For each paper, o3-mini writes 3 hypotheses that build on it, using teaching-text passages and MatKG facts as background; a critic (o3-mini, high reasoning effort) that sees the paper and background but never the question checks each for soundness, testability and going beyond the paper; the generator revises until at least one is accepted (at most 20 rounds, else the paper is dropped). The accepted hypotheses of all papers, near-duplicates merged, meet in a pairwise tournament on the question (o3-mini, high effort; both orders, a win needs both). Rank 1 is the final hypothesis.

broad.question: For transition-metal catalysts, formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability and why. Specify an unnamed controlled comparison that would reveal the governing cause, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an outcome that would falsify it.

problem_constrained.question: For nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts used in ethanol oxidation, strong reported performance has not yet yielded a comprehensive causal understanding of catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability under reaction conditions. Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs one of these behaviors and why. Specify an unnamed controlled change and an appropriate baseline, the predicted observations relative to that baseline, the operating boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify it.

expert_context.question: Platinum-group metals can promote distinct reactions, and earlier PGM-based nanoscale catalysts showed strong activity, selectivity, and durability in complex catalysis. A representative catalyst was reported to perform particularly well in ethanol oxidation, which involves 12-electron and 12-proton transfers, but these performance reports did not establish a comprehensive causal explanation of its behavior during operation. Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs its catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability and why. Define an unnamed controlled change with a suitable baseline, the predicted observations, the reaction regime in which the hypothesis should apply or fail, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive falsification outcome.
